title: 'Juuou Mujin Dandivine' Announces Additional Cast
content:
The official website for the Juuou Mujin Dandivine ( Beast King War God Dandivine ) original television anime announced additional cast members on Friday. The anime series is scheduled to premiere on October 8 at 12:30 a.m. on Tokyo MX, BS11, Gunma TV, Tochigi TV, followed by Chukyo TV and MBS.

Cast Haru: Nao Touyama ( Katainaka no Ossan, Kensei ni Naru ) Natsu: Aya Yamane ( Dandadan ) Aki: Misaki Kuno ( Reincarnation no Kaben ) Hori Sera: Asuna Tomari ( Towa no Yuugure ) Yuusaku Kuroiwa: Katsuyuki Konishi ( Gachiakuta ) Daigo Shijaku: Ryoutarou Okiayu ( Marriagetoxin )

• Genjuurou Shijaku: Atsushi Ono ( One Punch Man Season 2 )

Yuuga Shinonome: Ruriko Aoki ( Ore dake Level Up na Ken )

Yi Cao ( Dorohedoro episode director) is directing the anime at LIDENFILMS and Kayac Animation . Toshiki Inoue ( Ushio to Tora (TV)) is serving as series composition and script. Majiro ( Ryman's Club character design) is providing original character design, while robin is serving as animation character designer.

News submitted by Safuan12616
author: MyAnimeList

title: Now That I Can Control Reality With a Mouse Cursor Anime Anime Announced, Reveals First Trailer, Visual, October 4 Premiere
content:
Now That I Can Control Reality With A Mouse Cursor, I’m Gonna Click Away On The Girls! anime was officially announced, revealing the first trailer, visual, staff, and an October 4, 2026 premiere date. The anime will air on TOKYO MX and BS11 in Japan. The trailer released on YouTube is a censored version, while an uncensored “Premium Version” will stream through AnimeFesta.

The story follows Takumi, an otaku who notices during class that his mouse cursor has somehow moved beyond his computer screen and into reality. After discovering that he can actually control it, he begins experimenting with the ability, including using it on his former childhood friend Mone.

The anime is directed by Makoto Sokuza, with series composition by Eeyo Kurosaki. Studio HoKIBOSHI is handling the animation production, while Suiseisha is producing the series.

An illustration commemorating the anime adaptation was also released by original creator Okumaro, along with a message to viewers. In the message, Okumaro said they were genuinely surprised when they first learned that the series would receive an anime adaptation and expressed happiness at being able to bring the work to more people in a new format.

Okumaro thanked readers for their continued support and said they hope both existing manga readers and people discovering the series through the anime can enjoy it in their respective formats. They also encourage viewers to look forward to the new version of Mouse Cursor created by the anime’s staff and cast.
author: Anime Corner

title: Kagurabachi Anime Casts Miku Ito as Hinao, Miyari Nemoto as Char, New Character Trailers and Visuals Revealed
content:
KAGURABACHI anime revealed Miku Ito as Hinao and Miyari Nemoto as Char Kyonagi, along with new character visuals and individual trailers for both characters. The highly anticipated anime is set to premiere in April 2027, with Crunchyroll streaming it worldwide (excluding Japan, Mainland China, North Korea, and South Korea).

Studio Cypic is in charge of the animation production, with Tetsuya Takeuchi as the director. Takeuchi is famously known for the Rock Lee vs Gaara fight in Naruto. We previously also had the chance to interview CyberAgent’s Takahiro Yamauchi , who talked about the company and its goal of creating “ high-quality Japanese animation works that can be accepted globally .”

The main staff for the anime includes:

• Director: Tetsuya Takeuchi

• Character Design: Keigo Sasaki

• Production: Cypic

Previously, the anime revealed the following voice cast:

• Taihi Kimura as Chihiro Rokuhira

• Tomokazu Seki as Kunishige Rokuhira

• Katsuyuki Konishi as Togo Shiba

Hinao works at Cafe Haru Haru, where she serves as an intermediary connecting people looking for help with sorcerers. She takes Char under her protection and introduces her to Chihiro and the others.

Miku Ito Comment

Q. What are your impressions of the character you voice, and what did you keep in mind while voicing them?

I was directed to aim for natural, conversational dialogue that matched the overall tone of the series, so I focused on keeping my performance relaxed and natural. As for Hinao, I thought it would be fun to lean into her more comedic side every now and then, so whenever the opportunity arose, I tried to really embrace those moments and give them a little extra flavor. Everyone on the team has such a strong sense of dedication and respect for the series, so I’m really looking forward to continuing the recording sessions!

Q. How did you feel when you were cast, and what are your thoughts on the anime?

From the moment I started reading Kagurabachi, I found myself especially drawn to Hinao. She’s a rather unique character within the series, and I was fascinated by her from the very beginning. During the audition, I wondered whether I was truly capable of taking on the role, so I was absolutely overjoyed when I found out I’d been cast. I hope to portray Hinao in a way that makes her presence at “Cafe Haru Haru” feel like a comforting place within the anime as well. I’ll give it my all so that everyone comes to love the anime version of Hinao, too!

Q. What were your thoughts when you first read the manga?

Both the characters and the story are so gritty and cool! It felt like watching a movie. What struck me the most when reading the manga, though, was how beautifully the goldfish were depicted. I can’t wait to see how they are brought to life in the anime.

Q. What is Hinao’s greatest charm?

Hinao works as a sort of information broker, connecting the underworld with sorcerers. Even though she is well-versed in what seems like a dangerous world, she is incredibly cute and always remains completely natural and down-to-earth, which I think is wonderful. Her twin-bun hairstyle and casual clothes give her a bright, cheerful look, but she is also kind and very caring. There is something about her presence that makes you feel safe and at ease, which is another part of her charm. I also personally admire how effortlessly she can connect with anyone and treat everyone equally.

Q. How would you describe the appeal of the series in one phrase?

“Cool Japanese culture.” I’m sorry I couldn’t come up with anything catchier! Beyond the swords, battles, mental strength, and the bond between parent and child, I felt that the series is filled with little touches that are uniquely Japanese. Reading it honestly made me think, “Wow, Japan is so cool…”—which is why I chose this phrase!

Char is described as a cheerful and courageous young girl being pursued for certain reasons. Her claim that her pursuers possess “the most strongest sword” ultimately leads to her meeting Chihiro.

Miyari Nemoto Comment

Q. What are your impressions of the character you voice, and what did you keep in mind while voicing them?

Char’s lines are pretty short, so I felt a lot of pressure to express all of her emotions as honestly and concisely as possible! But once recording began, I found myself having a lot of fun voicing her.

Q. How did you feel when you were cast, and what are your thoughts on the anime?

When my manager told me in person at the agency that I’d been cast as Char, I let out such a loud noise that one of the staff members had to gently tell me to keep it down. Haha. Even then, until I actually had the script in my hands, I kept thinking, “Is it really… me…?” I was constantly bouncing between excitement and anxiety!

Q. What were your thoughts when you first read the manga?

It’s dark, but it also has the kind of optimism you’d expect from a Jump series. The comedy isn’t overly obvious either—it’s woven naturally into the serious moments. I also felt there was a real sense of style in how carefully the story flows as a whole. But honestly, I don’t know anything about the complicated stuff! I just know it’s incredibly fun to read!

Q. What is Char’s greatest charm?

Personally, I think she’s someone who naturally helps people relax. Even though she’s carrying a heavy burden herself, she’s usually full of energy. If Char isn’t cheerful, it makes everyone watching feel sad too… I think that’s part of what makes her so lovable. During recording, one of my senior castmates told me, “This role suits you perfectly.” I was just about to be happy when they added with a laugh, “…Because you’re the type who doesn’t read the room. Haha.” W-Wait, whaaaat!?!!

Q. How would you describe the appeal of the series in one phrase?

“Japanese swords are seriously cool.”

Following premiere screenings at Anime Expo in Los Angeles, Japan Expo in Paris, and AnimagiC in Germany, the anime also screened at Otakon in Washington, D.C. on August 2, before concluding the tour at Anime NYC later that month. Most events featured an advance screening of the first 20 minutes of Episode 1, with select venues also hosting staff and cast appearances.

The story follows the young Chihiro, who was trained by his father to become a swordsmith. After his father is murderer, Chihiro sets on a path of revenge to avenge him with yakuza and sorcerers standing against him. The official synopsis:

Flames of resolve, kindled by hatred. Chihiro Rokuhira is a boy who aspires to become a swordsmith, and took daily training under his father Kunishige, a renowned swordsmith. Their days, once filled with laughter, are brutally torn apart by an attack from the mysterious sorcerer organization, the Hishaku. What is stolen from them are the six Enchanted Blades—swords of immense power capable of shaping the fate of the nation—and the gentle, warm life they once shared. From that day on, everything changed. In a world engulfed in darkness, Chihiro takes up Enten, the seventh Enchanted Blade left behind by his father, and sets out on a blood-soaked path of revenge.

The first teaser trailer for the anime exceeded 6 million views within the first 24 hours, and you can check it out below.

title: Frontwing, Good Smile Co. Release Cocoro Visual Novel on Steam in English
content:
Frontwing and Good Smile Company released the Cocoro visual novel on Steam on Thursday. The game features text options in Japanese, English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese. The game retails for US$24.99 and is available for a 20% discount for a 12-day period after launch. A demo for the game is also available. In Japan the game is also available on DMM Games and DLsite.

Final Trailer

Opening Video

Frontwing describes the story of the visual novel:

"Please make me human." A sudden and unexplained global insurgence of AI has left the former utopian city of Tsukumo in ruins. Having lived there during his childhood, Hinata often hid at a botanical garden as his safe haven. There, he met a girl who helped him overcome his trauma, and he fell in love with her. On the day he left, he proposed to her. Upon returning to Tsukumo over summer break, Hinata hears rumors of a ghost in the now-abandoned botanical garden who is looking after the flowers. He goes to investigate and meets a humanoid girl who hopes to one day become human. "I may not look like much, but I actually have a fiancé. He promised to come here when those flowers bloom." Even as Hinata stands before her, she does not realize who he is. Thus, an unforgettable summer unfolds between a boy who has nowhere to call home and a humanoid girl who dreams of marriage…

The game stars:

• Hina Yomiya as Cocoro

• Hikaru Tōno as Ryuzaki Kazane

• Yasuaki Takumi as Amai Daichi

• Riona Imaizumi as Amai Kosame

• Maaya Uchida as Kizuki Kirika

• Shūta Morishima as Murakumo Kotaro

Asta Konno ( ATRI: My Dear Moments ) was in charge of planning and story for the game. Akio Watanabe ( Monogatari series) designed the characters, nanaca mai was in charge of SD art, y.ish was in charge of backgrounds, and Fuminori Matsumoto composed the music. yo-yu was in charge of the opening video. Runa Mizutani (Nanosize Mir) performs the opening theme song "Signal."
author: ANN

title: Arc System Works' Donutal Alien Immigration Simulation Game Reveals September 3 Debut in Trailer
content:
Arc System Works revealed on Thursday that it will release its upcoming Donutal game on PC via Steam on September 3 (September 4 in Japan). Arc System Works is also streaming a new character overview trailer for the game.

English version

Japanese version

Those who purchase the game between September 3 and November 30 will receive free future access to the game's soundtrack with 13 tracks.

The game takes place in 2206 and tasks players as a "Chief Extraterrestrial Counselor," screening aliens and selectively allowing Earth entry to aliens "who will advance Earth's future," while trying to deny entry to aliens "that could end the Earth." The gameplay is similar to the immigration simulation game Papers, Please .

The game's Steam page previously contained a disclaimer that notes that the game uses "AI-generated and post-retouched images for the illustrations accompanying some articles within the in-game 'news site.'" This disclaimer is no longer on the page.
author: ANN

title: Crunchyroll App on Nintendo Switch to be Discontinued on October 30
content:
Crunchyroll 's customer service page currently states that the service is not currently available for the Nintendo Switch 2 console. The page states, "At this time. the console does not support several video-on-demand services, which affects multiple video applications, including Crunchyroll ." Crunchyroll 's page also states it does not currently have any announcements about the service coming to Nintendo Switch 2 in the future.

Crunchyroll is still available on Xbox and PlayStation , as well as on mobile devices, media players, Smart TVs and TVs, service providers, and via web browsers.

Crunchyroll announced earlier this month it is collaborating with the automotive apps distribution platform Appning by FORVIA to enable its service to stream in select vehicles in North America, Latin America, Europe, Asia, India, and Australia. The collaboration will launch on BMW and MINI vehicles, then will expand across BMW Group vehicles and over 40 automotive brands.

Crunchyroll increased the prices for all of its subscription tiers in the U.S. in February, and Crunchyroll halted free ad-supported streaming on its service last December.

title: 'Kagurabachi' Announces Additional Cast Pair
content:
The official website for the television anime adaptation of Takeru Hokazono 's Kagurabachi manga revealed two additional cast and character promotional videos on Friday. The anime is scheduled to air in Spring 2027.

Voice actresses Miku Itou ( 5-toubun no Hanayome ) and Miyari Nemoto ( Ruri no Houseki ) are joining the cast as Hinao and Char Kyounagi, respectively.

Tetsuya Takeuchi ( Akuyaku Reijou Tensei Ojisan ) is directing the anime at Cypic . Keigo Sasaki ( Nantasu no Taizai ) is designing the characters. Shochiku and CyberAgent are producing the anime series.

Hokazono began serializing the action fantasy manga in Weekly Shounen Jump in September 2023. Shueisha published the 11th volume on May 1, with the 12th volume planned for a September 4 release. Kagurabachi has a cumulative 4 million copies of its volumes in circulation, including digital editions.

VIZ Media licensed the manga in English in March 2024 and published the eighth volume on August 4, with the ninth volume scheduled to be released on November 3. The company also simulpublishes it in English alongside Shueisha's Manga Plus platform.

Character PV (Char Kyounagi ver.)

News submitted by NokkiMal

title: Kagurabachi Anime Casts Miku Ito, Miyari Nemoto
content:
Shochiku , Crunchyroll , and CyberAgent Anime announced two more cast members for the television anime of Takeru Hokazono 's Kagurabachi manga with two English-subtitled character promotional videos on Friday:

Miyari Nemoto as Char Kyonagi, a cheerful and courageous young girl being pursued for certain reasons

Young Chihiro spends his days training under his famous swordsmith father. One day he hopes to become a great sword-maker himself. The goofy father and the serious son--they thought these days would last forever. But suddenly, tragedy strikes. A dark day soaked in blood. Chihiro and his blade now live only for revenge. Epic sword battle action!

The anime stars Taihi Kimura as Chihiro Rokuhira, Tomokazu Seki as Kunishige Rokuhira, and Katsuyuki Konishi as Togo Shiba.

Tetsuya Takeuchi ( From Bureaucrat to Villainess: Dad's Been Reincarnated! director; key animator for Naruto and Naruto Shippūden ) is directing the anime at Cypic ( The World Is Dancing ). Keigo Sasaki (character designer for Blue Exorcist , Uma Musume: Cinderella Gray ) is designing the characters. Shochiku and CyberAgent are on the production committee .

The anime will stream in April 2027 worldwide excluding Japan, Mainland China, North Korea, and South Korea.

The anime will premiere in April 2027, and will stream that month worldwide excluding Japan, Mainland China, North Korea, and South Korea. The "world tour" event for the anime began this past July at Anime Expo in Los Angeles, Japan Expo Paris in Paris, ANImagic in Mannheim, Germany, and in August at Anime NYC in New York. Viz Media is also releasing the manga in print and released the seventh volume on May 5.

The manga topped the print category in the Next Manga Awards 2024. The manga was nominated in December 2024 for the 70th Shogakukan Manga Awards, and was nominated for the 49th annual Kodansha Manga Awards in April 2025. The manga was also nominated for the 2025 Will Eisner Comic Industry Awards. The manga ranked at #13 in January for Da Vinci's top manga titles of 2025.

title: New Fairy Princess Minky Momo OVA Unveils 4 More Cast Members
content:
The official website for Mahō no Princess Minky Momo Akogare no Yume e Magokoro no Duo ( Fairy Princess Minky Momo A Duo of Sincerity Toward a Dream of Longing), the new original video anime ( OVA ) of the Fairy Princess Minky Momo magical girl anime franchise , announced four more cast members on Friday:

• Show Hayami as the King of Diginarsa

• Kikuko Inoue as the Queen of Diginarsa

• Kazuyuki Okitsu as Momo's kind father

• Mie Sonozaki as Momo's mother, who is a bit of a worrywart

The new OVA 's story is set in Diginarsa, the land of dreams and hopes, which maintains its existence through dream energy. But the land is in danger of disappearing as humans lose their dreams and hopes, and the dream energy decreases. As a last resort, the land's king sends off his three companions Chamocha, Dettabook, and Pipirupi to Min ky Momo for help.

On her 12th birthday, a girl named Momo received a smartphone as a present, and awakens as Min ky Momo after meeting the king's companions and resolves herself to save Diginarsa. As Momo steadily collects dream energy, a mysterious app begins to become popular in the city. But the dreams that children talk about in the app are nothing but frivolous dreams only driven by the desire for recognition or boosting their viewing numbers. Momo starts to question everyone's dreams.

The OVA stars:

• Kurumi Haruki as Minky Momo

• Fukushi Ochiai as Dettabook

• Natsumi Fujiwara as Chamocha

• Rie Kugimiya as Pipirupi

• Tomohito Takatsuka as Rubato

• Yōko Hikasa as Peter

Ayumu Watanabe ( Witch Hat Atelier , Akane-banashi , Space Brothers ) is directing the anime at Ashi Production . The original 1982-1983 anime's main animator Hiroshi Watanabe and Minky Momo in The Station of Your Memories key animator Mari Tominaga are designing the characters. Deko Akao ( Arakawa Under the Bridge two seasons, Pretty Rhythm Aurora Dream ) is writing the script, Katsunori Shimizu ( Magical Girl Ore , Citrus) is the sound director, Zack Promotion is in charge of sound production, and Tomoki Hasegawa ( Minky Momo in The Station of Your Memories , Cherry Magic! Thirty Years of Virginity Can Make You a Wizard?! ) is composing the music. Studio Live is credited for design cooperation. MOVIC and Giggly Box are distributing.

The new anime will open in theaters in Japan on November 13.

The new OVA will be the franchise 's first new one since 1994's Minky Momo in The Station of Your Memories , 32 years ago.

William Winckler Productions launched an Amazon Instant Video release of the 1982-1983 television anime as English-dubbed features in 2015, and it described the story:

In Minky Momo , a princess from a magical world is sent to Earth to help people recover their lost hopes and dreams. Using her magic, and with the aid of her magical dog, monkey and bird, Minky – known on Earth as “Gigi” – encounters amazing adventures.

The 1982-1983 series inspired a television series followup in 1991-1992 and several OVAs. Harmony Gold USA released the Fairy Princess Minky Momo: La ronde in my dream OVA in English as Gigi and the Fountain of Youth . Crunchyroll began streaming the original television anime in January 2024.

title: Bringing 'The Last Blossom' to Life: 'ODD TAXI' Team Returns with 'Housenka'
content:
Following their acclaimed work ODD TAXI , director Baku Kinoshita and writer Kazuya Konomoto return with Housenka ( The Last Blossom ), an original movie from animation studio CLAP and produced by Pony Canyon . Premiering in Japan on October 10, 2025 after its world debut at the Annecy International Film Festival 2025, the movie presents a grounded human story rooted in the realities of everyday life, with the fantastical touch of a talking flower that adds a bit of whimsy to its candid themes.

In this interview, we spoke with director Baku Kinoshita (middle), animation producer Ryoichiro Matsuo from CLAP (right), and producer Hirofumi Ito (left) from HI Production about the creative process behind Housenka , exploring the themes that make this movie a heartfelt and distinct addition to contemporary anime cinema.

See it in theatres on August 30 & 31 in the US & Canada!

──Can you briefly describe how this project began, and how each of you became a part of the film Housenka ?

Director Kinoshita: Even after our previous work ODD TAXI ended, I remained on friendly terms both personally and professionally with the scriptwriter, Kazuya Konomoto. So I thought that I wanted to work with him again, and I asked "Would you like to make an anime together?"

Producer Matsuo: This project began when I reached out to Director Kinoshita. When I worked with Director Kinoshita in the past, I thought he was a talented person who worked with great sincerity. So I got in touch with him because I wanted to make an interesting work together. Rather than "let's make Housenka ," the project started from the idea "let's make a work by Director Kinoshita."

Producer Ito: Originally, I worked with Director Kinoshita as a producer for ODD TAXI , and with CLAP as the chief producer for Natsu no Tunnel, Sayonara no Deguchi ( The Tunnel to Summer, the Exit of Goodbyes ). So I joined, thinking it would be great if the three of us could do something together.

──Kinoshita-san, in another interview, you mentioned that you had dreamed of creating a feature-length anime. Is Housenka the type of movie you envisioned for your first film?

Kinoshita: I think this work became one of the movies I had in mind. It feels like a dream I had imagined came into reality. I'm pleased that it turned into a very beautiful film.

──With both ODD TAXI and Housenka , the characters and their designs were created before the story was written. How does this process enable you and Konomoto-san to make such unique stories?

Kinoshita: The first time I worked with Konomoto-san was on ODD TAXI , and we used a process where the characters were created first and then the script was written afterwards. This approach was also an easier process for Konomoto-san to work with, so we adopted it for Housenka , too. Konomoto-san is the type of person who builds a story by using existing frames in a creative way, so I think this process was the best method.

──For a movie rooted firmly in reality, the fantastical addition of a talking flower is interesting. Was the flower one of the original characters envisioned for the story, and was it always a balsam ( housenka ) flower?

Kinoshita: From the beginning, it was decided that there would be a balsam ( housenka ) flower in the story, and that it would talk.

──Can you comment on what was considered when choosing the international title, The Last Blossom , instead of a reference to the flower's name.

Matsuo: When the film was submitted to the Annecy International Film Festival as a work in progress, it had the title Housenka . But after listening to everyone overseas and hearing opinions from various people, we decided that The Last Blossom was a more fitting title.

──There are two contrasting teaser visuals for the movie: darkness vs light, confinement vs freedom, present vs past, looking downcast vs up to the sky. Do you consider one to be more representative of the movie's main message (compared to the other)?

Kinoshita: I think both visuals together as a set express the essential aspects of the movie. It's a work that depicts the positives and negatives of life, so I think it's important to have the two as a set.

──So you see them more together as one rather than separate?

Kinoshita: I think you'll understand when you watch the movie, but the film was constructed so that confined spaces and free spaces alternate with a balanced appearance of about 50% each. So in that sense, two key visuals were necessary.

──Artist Michinoku-Toge commented that he was directed to make the prison cell feel peaceful and gentle, rather than cold and uninviting like one might expect. What were your thoughts behind this direction?

Kinoshita: If you draw a prison cell as cold and lifeless as it really is, then it will give a gray impression. And if a scene with a gray impression continues for a long time, the movie screen will end up being dull and dreary. But this time, I didn't want the film to be gloomy, so I decided to make the beauty of the moonlight be felt even inside the prison.

──At the Annecy Festival, you told the audience "Everyone who sees this will feel good today." When approaching very human topics like this, is it important to you that the audience leaves with a positive outlook?

Kinoshita: Yes, I think it's very important. In the end, it's important that watching a movie forms a new sense of your inner values, even if only a little. Likewise, I think leaving a film with a refreshed feeling is a really important part of the movie-going experience.

──Are there any moments or scenes in the film that made you feel personally fulfilled as a director (or producer)? Such as additions that weren't in the script.

Kinoshita: Fundamentally, the film is faithful to the script and not much was changed. It's a very minor detail, but there is a scene where the henchman of a character named Tsutsumi is playing by tossing cigarettes by the roadside that wasn't in the script. The scene is a fun, palate cleanser and makes me laugh a little, so I like it.

Ito: From a producer's perspective, it's the music. While I can't say the names yet, everyone got together to discuss and select the songs, and I think the music that plays during the end credits is one of the distinctive features of this work.

Translator's Note: The song has since been announced as "Stand By Me" by cero feat. Manami Kakudo.

──In his cast comment, Kaoru Kobayashi mentioned recording alone with Pierre Taki, and how both of them found it difficult to unwind after the session. Were these recordings also memorable or impactful for you?

Kinoshita: I didn't hear anything specifically from Kobayashi Kaoru-san or Pierre Taki-san, but during the recording, I got the impression that both of them used up a lot of calories. Kobayashi Kaoru-san in particular kept saying, "I'm tired. I'm tired." For two days straight, he played the role of a dying old man so that's probably why he felt extremely emotional and tired.

──Can you comment on the usage of pre-scoring in your works, and if you consider this an important element for bringing your characters to life.

Kinoshita: Pre-scoring was used for both ODD TAXI and Housenka . With pre-scoring, first we ask the actors to perform their lines freely without any time constraints, and then the animators add illustrative performances to the characters after. I think this way you can create animation that feels more like it's clinging or attached to the characters. It's a method that is not often used in Japan.

──Matsuo-san, you've mentioned before that you've "learned the importance of not only creating works but also steadily promoting them." Did you face any difficulties regarding the promotion of the film, Housenka ?

Matsuo: Since it's an original work, when promoting it, first of all I thought it was important to have a wide variety of people watch it. This time as well, we were hoping to spread awareness by submitting it to overseas film festivals. Our goal was to hold the world premiere screening at the Annecy Film Festival, so that as many people as possible could see it. Then, so that what people watched would spread, the director, producer—everyone worked together to build upon various aspects.

Many works are promoted first in Japan and then released overseas, but promotion for this film began spreading quickly from overseas. In June last year it was shown at Annecy, in July it was teased at Anime Expo, and then in the fall it was released in Japan. By having a variety of people see it and spread the word before the premiere, we can generate a current that makes people think, "I want to see it right away." To make it in time for the film festival, the director and entire team worked hard to complete the movie until the very last minute.

Translator's Note: Studio CLAP's previous film, Natsu no Tunnel, Sayonara no Deguchi , was featured at the 2023 Annecy Film Festival where it won the Paul Grimault Award.

The Last Blossom exhibit at Anime Expo 2025 (Pony Canyon booth)

──Given how emotionally charged Housenka is, how did everyone feel after the movie was finished and ready to premiere?

Kinoshita: I think Housenka is more about artistry than commerciality, so I'm really happy to be able to make such a beautifully, sincere film at this time. I can't wait for everyone to see it.

Matsuo: I followed the production closely, but when it was completed along with the music, I thought a truly memorable work had been created. It turned out to be such a wonderful film that I wanted lots of people to see it, and for them to watch it over and over again.

Ito: Although this work has a plain, unflashy title, I thought once again when it was completed how grateful I am to both of these men, for creating a work that will leave a strong impression on my grandchildren even five or ten years from now. (I don't have any grandchildren yet though.)

──MyAnimeList's community has rated ODD TAXI as one of the Top 100 anime of all time, and I think many overseas fans are eagerly anticipating this film. Is there anything you would like to say to them?

Kinoshita: Just like with ODD TAXI , this film was made by Kazuya Konomoto and I. So everyone can have high expectations that Kazuya Konomoto's script will have plenty of gimmicks and interesting dialogue, and I hope everyone will watch it.

Interview was conducted through an interpreter and has been edited for clarity.
